label: copy-phase echoed v when the next output is v or a (late positions)
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.005% of steps). All activations are in the copy phase on steps where the input is the fed-back token v. The feature never fires in the original or delimiter phase or on any other input token. Within that, about 97% of activations (98% of mass) come when the token being output is v (repeated v, e.g. ...v v a, 77% of mass) or a (v followed by a, 21%). They come at recall_idx >= 3, so the v sits at original position >= 2, and rate and magnitude are highest in long sequences (L=9 holds 48% of mass). The strongest examples come from originals with a v v a run in mid-sequence, firing on the first echoed v. However, the feature is unreliable even in this context: only about 8% of matching steps activate, and nearly identical sequences (e.g. ...2 v v a) often stay silent, so precision is low. Rare misses are v followed by c or w.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 37 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=v (+3.18), in_tok=v (+2.70), phase=2 & out_tok=v (+2.43), out_tok=v (+2.33), phase=2 & out_tok=a (+2.23), next_out=a (+1.93). Lower it: in_count=1 (-3.18), in_count=2 (-1.84), orig0=v (-1.77), prev2_tok=d (-1.56).
